pages.title: Start with one machine
pages.text: Confirm the ME network has power, a free channel and storage space, then connect the machine with cable. On the Items page of side configuration enable A (AE output); enable I only when the centrifuge should fetch materials itself. A fresh connection will not immediately drain storage.

pages.title: Where the input window lives
pages.text: Open the centrifuge, click Side Configuration at the top left, switch to the Items page, then click the I button in the second cell of the left column (tooltip "AE2 input config"). The window floats over the machine; close it with the top-left x or Esc (a pinned window ignores Esc).

pages.title: The control row
pages.text: I toggles pulling; N toggles NBT ignore (keep matching for configurable combs); F cycles the filter mode disabled/whitelist/blacklist; P toggles precise mode (on separates combs from comb blocks, off shares one quota); the gear edits all pull amounts; Stock edits the global reserve; T opens tag expressions. On the right, < C > page and clear.

pages.title: Per-cell actions
pages.text: Each cell stacks gear, marker and network output from top to bottom. Carry an item and left- or right-click the marker to add it; empty-hand click a filled marker to remove it; JEI drag also works. Gear: left-click sets the pull amount, right-click toggles stock mode, Shift+left-click toggles unlimited, Shift+right-click sets the reserve. The output row takes from or inserts into the network.

pages.title: Safe input test
pages.text: Start with one comb, a small pull amount (1-4) and a network reserve so the last emergency stack stays in storage. Note that a reserve higher than the network stock pulls nothing at all. A cell with a grey overlay means this machine has no recipe for that comb, so the entry will never take effect.

pages.title: Cooldown and troubleshooting
pages.text: The Cooldown line is adaptive: a successful pull returns it to 5 ticks (1 tick for unlimited entries), a pull that misses its quota backs off to 10, and a pull that gets nothing can back off to 40. A cooldown stuck at 40 usually means there is nothing pullable in the network.

pages.title: Power priority
pages.text: Machines can receive FE through the connected network. With Applied Flux installed, keep "Prefer Applied Flux" enabled to use FE stored in the network first. Disable "Native AE Energy Input" only when the machines must use Applied Flux FE exclusively. A disconnected network pauses safely without deleting machine contents.

pages.title: Avoid network stalls
pages.text: Give products and fluids enough storage. If a large network starts stuttering, lower the pull amount or increase the pull interval. Change one setting at a time and watch whether machine inputs remain stable before increasing throughput again.
